::: {.why}
Point-in-time is not a data-cleaning nicety; it is the difference between a research result and a result you obtained by reading tomorrow's newspaper, and it is the design constraint for everything you build from day 20.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the difference between an observation date and an effective date, and give a series where they differ by months.
- Write the as-of query in SQL: given a fact table with both dates, return what was knowable on an arbitrary date.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Look at your two ALFRED vintages properly. Tabulate, for one quarter of GDP, the first published value and the value as it stands now, and the gap in months between the quarter ending and the first print. Then say what a backtest that used the current series would have known in advance.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Write the as-of query as SQL against a two-date fact table: select the latest row per entity where observation_date is less than or equal to the as-of date. Get it right for the case where a fact is revised twice, and for the case where a fact is deleted.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the design decision into reports/milestone-01-market-map.md: every table in your store carries the date the fact refers to and the date you learned it, and no query is allowed to omit the second.
:::
:::
